source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Dividend is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Can the learner divide by a decimal divisor by scaling both dividend' is answered as dividend rather than decimal divisor.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Dividend is what produces decimal divisor, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Can the learner divide by a decimal divisor by scaling.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: decimal divisor is settled by running 'Can the learner convert a fraction to a terminating decimal by finding': A fraction can be written as a terminating decimal when it is changed to an equivalent — on the item about Can the learner divide by a decimal divisor by scaling.

mx.name: operation_confusion
mx.teacher_note: Decimal divisor is found by dividing the given values instead of multiplying, giving 41 as the reported result — on the item about Can the learner divide by a decimal divisor by scaling.

intelligence.enrichment: When the divisor is a decimal, multiply both divisor and dividend by the same power of 10 to make the divisor a counting number, then divide using place value.
